rationale: C04 plausibly supplied the central drafting pattern: a short executive order suspending the operation of a statutory requirement until a specified date, in an Army-related setting. Its language—describing a law as “suspend[ed] until” a fixed date and using “is hereby”—closely parallels the child’s operative suspension. C03 exactly shares the effective-date sentence, but that is a routine clause and insufficient by itself. C12 also uses a temporary statutory-relief mechanism ending June 30, 1948, but its proclamation structure and trademark-specific machinery are less similar.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The operation of all provisions of law requiring professional examinations ... is hereby suspended until June 30, 1948.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: which suspends until July 1, 1948, the eight-hour law as to all work performed by laborers and mechanics employed by the Department of the Army ... is hereby amended
shared_material.explanation: Both employ concise presidential language temporarily suspending a legal requirement until a fixed mid-1948 date, with direct connection to the Army.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This order shall become effective as of January 1, 1948.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The penultimate paragraph of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] ... is hereby amended
shared_material.explanation: Both are brief operative orders framed as immediate modifications of otherwise governing legal requirements, although the child's express retroactive-effective-date clause is not present in C04.
